newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher, recovering as Dow rises.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher, recovering as Dow rises.

text.p: Brazilian stocks erased steep losses Monday afternoon to close 0.02 percent higher, aided by a recovery on Wall Street and the decision by some investors not to exercise options with prices so low, brokers said.
"People saw New York was closing higher, and we had some buy orders in the afternoon," said a trader at local Indusval brokerage.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 most-traded shares rose three points to end up 11,337 points in total turnover of 2.027 billion reais ($1.87 billion).
Brokers said the bolsa, off more than three percent by midafternoon, began recovering as many holders of Telebras options holders decided to place buy orders instead of selling.

The mood swing was spurred by a rebound on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 1.41 percent higher, they said. On Friday, the Dow fell three percent and the Bovespa ended 4.78 percent lower.
"There was no news, so it was just speculation really," one dealer said, referring to Monday's activity. "There was a recovery in New York and a partial recovery here."

Brokers said the session's volume, while significantly higher than the daily average because of Monday's expiration of options, was sharply lower than turnover experienced on other recent options expiration dates.
Telebras, which normally accounts for 65 percent of daily trade, ended 1.46 percent higher Monday at 139 reais while its common closed 1.14 percent higher at 124.40 reais.
Its rise, however, failed to spur rallies in other key blue chips.
State-owned oil company Petrobras' preferred ended down 2.33 percent at 294 reais while the federal power holding company Eletrobras preferred B closed off 2.75 percent at 530.01 reais.
Cia Vale do Rio Doce, the recently privatized mining company, rose 2.4 percent at 26.01 reais.
